dedupe_keys.name: simulating on demand feeder transport around varginha station sao paulo matsim eqasim

description: This case covers a preliminary study by FGV Cidades that simulated an on-demand transport service integrated with the bus and rail network around the new Varginha station in the south of São Paulo. The team used agent-based models in MATSim with the eqasim framework, which keep full city-wide routing, and tested fleets of 50, 100 and 200 vehicles, waiting and detour rules, spatial limits to avoid overlapping bus lines and service in areas without nearby stops. For existing train and bus users who switched to the on-demand feeder, waiting time fell by about 50% and walking by about 30%, while the service carried under 4% of daily trips even at 200 vehicles and cut total kilometres driven by about 6% by drawing users from cars and ride-hailing. The most efficient setup served 27,500 accepted rides a day at about R$21 per passenger, and a 200-vehicle operation was estimated at R$12 to 14 million a month. The results were published as a column on Caos Planejado in October 2025. Coverage is the area around one station in São Paulo. Access: the article is free to read; the model and data are not published with it. Limitations: the authors call the results preliminary and simulation-only. It is related to MATSim catalogued here.
name: Simulating on-demand feeder transport around Varginha station, São Paulo (MATSim/eqasim)
outcomes: About 50% less waiting and 30% less walking for switching public transport users, under 4% of daily trips served, about 6% fewer vehicle kilometres, and about R$21 per passenger in the best setup.
